launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.address: Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA 94117
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.summary: Golden Gate Park is San Francisco's 1,017-acre, three-mile-long destination park, with museums, gardens, lakes, playgrounds, meadows, sports, wildlife, and the car-free JFK Promenade.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.hours: The park is open daily from 5 a.m. to midnight. Museums, gardens, playgrounds, restrooms, concessions, roads, shuttles, and events use separate schedules.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.cost: General park landscapes, trails, meadows, playgrounds, and lakes are free. Museums, gardens, rentals, food, events, and selected parking charge separately.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.parking: Choose parking for the exact destination. Street spaces, attraction garages, and small lots are distributed across a park three miles long; events and car-free roads change access.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.arrival: Use Stanyan Street for the east end, 9th Avenue for Music Concourse, 25th Avenue for central destinations, or the Great Highway for the west end. Do not route to the park center.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.restrooms: Restrooms are distributed near major attractions, playgrounds, sports areas, and concessions and do not all keep park hours. Identify the closest facility on the visitor map.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.accessibility: The City publishes a most-usable-pathways map and operates a free park shuttle. Grades, historic paths, attraction entrances, and event detours vary by destination.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.dogs: Dogs follow posted leash and dog-play-area rules and are restricted from playgrounds, fields during play, museums, gardens, and sensitive habitat.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.family: Koret Children's Quarter, the carousel, lakes, gardens, museums, and meadows make this a full family day, but distances and separate attraction schedules require a plan.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.transit: Muni serves several edges of the park, and the free park shuttle connects major destinations. Choose transit for the attraction rather than a generic park stop.
launch-ca-san-francisco-golden-gate-park.need: Expect strong west-side wind, fog, microclimates, event closures, and long distances. Check the exact attraction schedule and current road access before leaving.

launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.summary: The Presidio is a 1,500-acre national park site with Tunnel Tops, the Outpost playground, beaches, forests, trails, historic Main Post, overlooks, museums, food, and free shuttles.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.hours: The Presidio grounds are open 24 hours daily. The Visitor Center is generally open 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.; playgrounds, museums, food, beaches, shuttles, and restrooms use separate schedules.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.cost: Park admission, Tunnel Tops, the Outpost, trails, overlooks, and Presidio GO are free. Paid parking, museums, lodging, food, golf, camping, and programs cost separately.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.parking: Paid parking is distributed near major destinations, with accessible spaces at Tunnel Tops, the Visitor Center, Crissy Field, and other areas. Baker Beach has two free lots.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.arrival: Start at Presidio Visitor Center and Tunnel Tops for orientation, or route directly to Baker Beach, Fort Point, a trailhead, or an overlook. The park is too large for one useful pin.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.restrooms: Accessible restrooms are available at Presidio Transit Center, Tunnel Tops near the Outpost, the Visitor Center area, beaches, and staffed destinations; hours vary.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.accessibility: Tunnel Tops has flat routes and two wheelchair-accessible north-south paths. Accessible parking and the wheelchair-accessible Presidio GO serve major areas; natural trails vary.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed in many outdoor areas but not playgrounds or indoor facilities; beaches and habitat areas have location-specific rules.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.family: Tunnel Tops combines the Outpost nature playground, Field Station, lawns, picnic tables, restrooms, food vendors, and bridge views in the easiest family base.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.transit: Free Presidio GO routes connect downtown and destinations inside the park. Muni 30 and 43 also serve the Main Post and Tunnel Tops area.
launch-ca-san-francisco-the-presidio.need: Main Post access and safety construction runs from July 2026 into winter 2027, bringing detours, noise, and traffic. Check shuttle alerts, wind, fog, beach surf, and destination closures.

launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.address: 19th and Dolores Streets, San Francisco, CA 94114
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.summary: Mission Dolores Park is a nearly 16-acre neighborhood landmark with sloped lawns, skyline views, an accessible playground, courts, soccer, picnic space, restrooms, and two dog areas.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.hours: Park hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Restrooms are 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in spring and summer and 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. in fall and winter.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.cost: General park, playground, lawns, courts, field, and dog areas are free. Reservations, permits, concessions, and special events may charge.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.parking: There is no destination lot. Street parking is scarce; use the J Church, nearby buses, walking, cycling, or rideshare and expect event-day restrictions.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.arrival: Use Church and 20th Streets for Helen Diller Playground and upper views. Lower entrances near Dolores and 18th are closer to courts and flatter lawn areas.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.restrooms: The park has public restrooms, but they close earlier than the park and use seasonal hours: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. spring/summer and 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. fall/winter.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.accessibility: The listed accessible children's play area and developed paths are useful, but steep lawns and grades between 18th and 20th Streets affect routes.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.dogs: Two off-leash dog play areas are provided. Dogs must remain controlled and follow leash rules outside designated zones and stay out of playgrounds and active fields.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.family: Helen Diller Playground is the primary family destination; the rest of the park is open, busy, sloped, and unfenced, requiring supervision around crowds and streets.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.transit: The J Church runs along the west edge, with buses and BART connections nearby. Transit is usually easier than searching for parking.
launch-ca-san-francisco-mission-dolores-.need: Sunny afternoons and events create dense crowds. Bring layers, pack out trash, watch valuables, and confirm restroom hours before an evening visit.

launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.address: 680 Point Lobos Avenue, San Francisco, CA 94121
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.summary: Lands End is a rugged oceanfront park of cliffside trails, cypress woods, Golden Gate views, Sutro Baths ruins, memorials, beaches, and historic batteries.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.hours: Outdoor trails and overlooks follow posted Golden Gate National Recreation Area access. Lands End Lookout, restrooms, parking, and nearby attractions have separate hours.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.cost: Trails, overlooks, Sutro Baths ruins, memorials, and general outdoor access are free. Parking and nearby attractions or food may cost separately.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.parking: Merrie Way near Lands End Lookout is the primary lot and fills quickly. Legion of Honor and Fort Miley approaches serve different trail sections; do not expect one lot to fit every route.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.arrival: Start at Lands End Lookout for Sutro Baths and western trail access. Use El Camino del Mar for the USS San Francisco Memorial, Legion of Honor, and eastern trail sections.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.restrooms: Restrooms are concentrated near Lands End Lookout and selected developed facilities. There are no dependable facilities on remote trail or beach sections.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.accessibility: Wheelchair-accessible trails begin at the Merrie Way parking lot, but stairs, steep grades, sand, roots, and cliffside natural paths limit many routes.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.dogs: Follow current GGNRA leash and habitat rules. Keep dogs controlled near cliffs, stairs, wildlife, crowded overlooks, and narrow trail traffic.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.family: The Lookout, Sutro Baths overlook, and short accessible paths work for many families; long stairs to beaches and cliffside trails require close supervision.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.transit: Muni serves Point Lobos Avenue and nearby Richmond District stops. Transit avoids the most competitive parking at Lands End Lookout.
launch-ca-san-francisco-lands-end.need: Stay on marked trails and away from cliff edges. Expect wind, fog, slippery steps, poison oak, weak cell coverage, cold surf, and rapidly changing coastal weather.

launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.address: 1199 East Beach Road, San Francisco, CA 94129
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.summary: Crissy Field is a restored bayfront destination with East Beach, a level promenade, marsh habitat, picnic areas, lawns, bridge views, the Warming Hut, and Fort Point connections.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.hours: Outdoor shoreline and promenade access follows posted GGNRA hours. Parking, restrooms, the Warming Hut, programs, and staffed facilities use separate schedules.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.cost: Beach, promenade, lawns, marsh overlooks, picnic areas, and general access are free. Parking, food, rentals, and programs may charge.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.parking: Paid parking serves East Beach and West Bluff, including accessible spaces. Lots fill on warm weekends and major event days; choose the end closest to your activity.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.arrival: Use East Beach for sand, large picnic sites, beach mat, and dog wash. Use West Bluff for the Warming Hut, Torpedo Wharf, and the shorter Fort Point approach.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.restrooms: Accessible restrooms are at East Beach, West Bluff near the Warming Hut, and Golden Gate Bridge Plaza. Drinking water is also available at these developed areas.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.accessibility: The 2.3-mile promenade is generally level with accessible parking and restrooms at both ends. East Beach offers a seasonal beach mat and beach wheelchairs by request.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.dogs: Dog access varies by shoreline and habitat zone. Follow posted leash controls, protect marsh wildlife, and use the designated dog-washing station at East Beach.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.family: East Beach combines sand, picnic tables, grills, restrooms, water, and a generally level promenade, making it the easiest family base.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.transit: Muni, Presidio GO, cycling, and walking connect Crissy Field with the Main Post and city. Stops may still require a waterfront walk.
launch-ca-san-francisco-crissy-field.need: Bay water is cold and conditions change quickly. Check wind, fog, tides, air quality, event closures, and parking; watch children closely near the shoreline and bicycle traffic.

launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.summary: Yerba Buena Gardens is a free downtown cultural landscape with lawns, the MLK Memorial waterfall, public art, children's play, gardens, museums, a carousel, and year-round events.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.hours: The gardens are open daily 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Public restrooms are open daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.; museums, carousel, play areas, food, and events keep separate schedules.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.cost: Garden admission, lawns, public art, and many programs are free. Museums, carousel, skating, bowling, food, parking, and selected events charge separately.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.parking: There is no free garden lot. Use BART, Muni, walking, cycling, or a paid SoMa garage; conventions and downtown events sharply increase demand.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.arrival: Use 750 Howard Street for the Esplanade. Children's attractions are south of Howard, while museums and convention access surround the north garden blocks.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.restrooms: Public restrooms are open seven days a week from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., shorter than garden hours. Partner attractions have separate customer facilities.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.accessibility: Developed garden paths, elevators, ramps, and adjacent cultural facilities provide multiple routes, but event setups and the multi-block layout can change circulation.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.dogs: Follow posted garden rules and keep pets controlled around lawns, children's areas, fountains, food, public art, and crowded events. Service animals are allowed where required.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.family: The children's garden, play circle, carousel, Creativity Museum, lawns, and nearby food form a strong downtown family cluster, with separate hours and fees.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.transit: Powell Street and Montgomery BART/Muni stations and numerous buses are within walking distance. Transit is usually easier than parking.
launch-ca-san-francisco-yerba-buena-gard.need: Garden access is free, but attractions and restroom hours differ. Check conventions, festivals, rain, wind, fountain maintenance, and the live event calendar.

launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.summary: Salesforce Park is a free 5.4-acre rooftop public park with a half-mile botanical loop, lawns, amphitheater, fountains, children's play, public art, and frequent free programming.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.hours: May through October hours are 6 a.m. to 9 p.m.; November through April hours are 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. Hours are subject to change.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.cost: Park admission and public programming are free unless an event states otherwise. Food, parking, and transit fares cost separately.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.parking: Use transit or a paid downtown garage; the park has no free visitor lot. Traffic and garage access are difficult during commute hours and events.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.arrival: The main entrance is Salesforce Plaza at 425 Mission and Fremont. Five elevator banks and one escalator reach the rooftop across the four-block Transit Center.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.restrooms: Public restrooms are inside the Transit Center rather than spread through the rooftop. Confirm the nearest open facility and elevator before settling at the far end.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.accessibility: Elevators connect street and transit levels to the rooftop, and the principal loop is developed. Elevator outages and event setups can change the best entrance.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.dogs: Pets are not allowed because of the park's delicate plant habitat. Service animals are allowed.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.family: The children's play area, fountains, lawns, botanical loop, and free activities work well for families, but the long rooftop needs a meeting point and restroom plan.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.transit: The park sits atop the regional Transit Center, served by bus operators and nearby Muni/BART connections. Street-level access varies by operator and time.
launch-ca-san-francisco-salesforce-park.need: Confirm park hours, elevator status, wind, heat, rain, and event occupation. Use a named elevator bank when meeting others because the park spans nearly four blocks.

launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.address: Hayes and Steiner Streets, San Francisco, CA 94117
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.summary: Alamo Square is a photogenic hilltop park with the Painted Ladies view, lawns, accessible playground, dog area, tennis court, picnic space, gardens, paths, and restrooms.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.hours: Park hours are 5 a.m. to midnight. Restrooms are 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in spring and summer and 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. in fall and winter.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.cost: Park, overlook, playground, dog area, lawn, and general recreation are free. Permits, reservations, tours, parking, and nearby food may cost.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.parking: There is no park lot. Street parking is scarce and tour activity affects loading; use Muni, walking, cycling, or rideshare when possible.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.arrival: Use Steiner Street for the classic Painted Ladies view. The accessible entrance is at the southeast corner at Hayes and Scott Streets.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.restrooms: Accessible public restrooms use seasonal hours: 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. spring/summer and 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. fall/winter.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.accessibility: The designated accessible entrance is at Hayes and Scott. The park is a hilltop, so routes from other corners can involve significant grades.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.dogs: A designated off-leash dog play area is provided. Dogs must be leashed elsewhere and controlled around playgrounds, lawns, picnics, and crowds.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.family: The dual-level accessible playground, lawns, picnic space, and short walking loop make a good neighborhood stop; hills and surrounding streets require supervision.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.transit: Muni buses serve the surrounding Western Addition and Hayes Valley streets. Transit avoids limited curb parking.
launch-ca-san-francisco-alamo-square.need: The famous view attracts tours and crowds. Protect valuables, respect residential stoops, check restroom hours, and bring layers for exposed hilltop wind.

launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.address: Ocean Beach, Great Highway, San Francisco, CA 94122
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.summary: Ocean Beach is a 3.5-mile Pacific shoreline for walking, kites, sunsets, surfing, wildlife, and seasonal fires, with dangerous cold water and strong currents.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.hours: The beach follows posted GGNRA access; City-managed parking lots close at 10 p.m. Seasonal fires must end by 9:30 p.m. and are prohibited November through February.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.cost: Beach and promenade access are free. Parking, food, rentals, permits, and transit fares may cost.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.parking: Lots and curb areas are spread along the shoreline and close at 10 p.m. Sunset Dunes changed vehicle circulation on the former Upper Great Highway, so route to the chosen stairwell.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.arrival: Choose the north end near Kelly's Cove, central stairwells 15 to 20 for legal seasonal fire rings, or the Sloat Boulevard area for southern access.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.restrooms: Restroom coverage is limited and widely spaced. Identify an open facility near the chosen stairwell or adjacent developed area before settling on the beach.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.accessibility: Accessible routes connect selected parking areas to the promenade, and beach wheelchairs are available by request. Sand and dynamic shoreline conditions remain limiting.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.dogs: Dog rules vary by season and zone. The snowy plover protection area south of stairwell 21 requires a leash no longer than six feet from July 1 through May 15.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.family: The beach is excellent for walking, kites, and sand play, but the water is frigid with dangerous currents and no assumption of lifeguard protection.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.transit: Muni serves several east-west corridors ending near the beach. Sunset Dunes improves walking and cycling access but changes driving routes.
launch-ca-san-francisco-ocean-beach.need: Do not treat Ocean Beach as a casual swimming beach. Check surf, tides, fog, wind, cold, air quality, and plover rules. Fires are only in provided rings March through October, with no glass or alcohol.

launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.address: Great Highway between Lincoln Way and Sloat Boulevard, San Francisco, CA 94122
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.summary: Sunset Dunes is San Francisco's two-mile, 50-acre car-free oceanfront park with walking and cycling, skate and bike features, fitness, children's nature play, seating, hammocks, art, and events.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.hours: Park hours are 5 a.m. to midnight. Temporary restrooms, programs, construction areas, and pop-up amenities use separate schedules.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.cost: General park, promenade, seating, public art, and permanent outdoor features are free. Programs, vendors, permits, parking, and rentals may cost.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.parking: Private vehicles are not allowed on the park promenade. Use neighborhood transit, walking, cycling, rideshare, or legal parking near a named cross street without blocking residents.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.arrival: Choose Lincoln Way for the Golden Gate Park end, Judah for the central activity hub, Noriega for the temporary restroom, or Sloat for the south end. The park is two miles long.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.restrooms: A temporary public restroom is located at Noriega. Do not assume restroom coverage at every entrance; identify the closest open facility before a long walk.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.accessibility: The former roadway provides a broad, generally level promenade, with access conditions varying at cross streets and temporary installations.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.dogs: Dogs must follow posted leash, waste, habitat, and event rules. Keep pets away from restored dunes, wildlife, children's play, and fast bicycle traffic.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.family: Nature play, skate and bike features, art, seating, and the broad car-free route are family-friendly. Shipwreck Cove is under installation and expected later in 2026, not yet guaranteed open.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.transit: Muni lines reach several west-side cross streets. Pick the stop closest to the desired section rather than walking the full two miles unexpectedly.
launch-ca-san-francisco-sunset-dunes.need: Expect wind, fog, sand, limited shelter, and construction changes. Shipwreck Cove installation began in July 2026 with expected completion around September; confirm opening before promising it to children.
